A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same detokenization and inner-lexicon study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original word/nonword classification, word-retrieval, attention, and vocabulary-expansion experiments, with additional analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical studies and adds FFN interventions, further probing experiments, biomedical and Arabic evaluations, and token-reduction measurements.

M1.justification: Section 6 replaces v1's identity/linear-regression expansion approaches with orthogonal Procrustes mappings and a new refinement stage. Two zero-initialized residual matrices are jointly trained through continued pretraining while original model weights remain frozen. This materially changes the vocabulary-expansion procedure.

E1.justification: Vocabulary-expansion evaluation extends from WikiText-103 to biomedical PubMed abstracts and Arabic Wiki40B. v3 also evaluates morphologically plausible ARC nonwords and adds country-capital recall under interventions, substantially broadening domains, language coverage, and tasks.

E2.justification: The principal expansion comparator changes substantially: v1's last-token input-embedding baseline is replaced by Mean Embed., following Gee et al. (2022), which initializes both input and output entries from average token embeddings within the revised framework. The original unexpanded model remains a baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes its stated input from words without context to words with 100 preceding tokens; this establishes a reported setting revision, not necessarily a rerun. Section 6 introduces corpus-based refinement training and dataset-specific frequency thresholds. Table 1 drops MRR and changes accuracy reporting to new-token, original-or-new-token, and all-token categories.

E4.justification: v3 adds targeted-versus-random FFN ablations testing word reconstruction and capital recall, ARC and cross-model checks of word/nonword probing, and cosine-similarity validation (Section 5.1; Appendices A, E, F). The prefix-token control already existed in v1. Its detailed positive-prediction breakdown and the earlier identity-versus-linear/input-only expansion comparisons are not retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the same two one-sided t-tests per layer, significance threshold, and Table 3 p-values. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, or confidence intervals, and v3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 is replaced: v1 reports WikiText Fused-Linear (E+U) accuracy of 56.7% on original tokens and 19.5% on new words; v3 reports all-token accuracies of 51.9%, 51.1%, and 53.2% on WikiText, PubMed, and Arabic under changed methods and scoring. These are not comparable performance gains. New results include intervention effects and 10.5–14.5% encoding-token reductions, while many retrieval curves and Table 3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix G introduces explicit mapping objectives with the orthogonality constraint T-transpose T = I and states the resulting distance-preservation property. This adds a restricted mathematical formulation beyond v1's generic linear-regression description. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: early-to-middle-layer detokenization, whole-word representations at the final token, an inner lexicon beyond tokenizer vocabulary, and vocabulary expansion without changing pretrained core weights. Clarifications about previously unseen input representations are consistent with v1's body; new experiments mainly strengthen supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets the inner lexicon as a soft representation assembled from multiple vectors and potentially retrieved in multiple layers. Targeted interventions support a stronger necessity argument for FFN updates than v1's observational evidence. Appendix H adds a substantive applicability limitation: only 16.0% of attempted Arabic words yield usable detokenized representations, suggesting incomplete lexical coverage.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly documents vocabulary-state extraction, the Procrustes implementation, RMS normalization, and rescaling. Section 6 specifies refinement initialization, sequence length, sequence count, and approximate single-GPU training time. Code availability changes from a promised release to a stated release. However, the stated 20M-token budget is not reconciled with the footnote specifying 10,000 sequences of length 512.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds focused connections to concept geometry through Park et al. and a new inner-lexicon-structure paragraph. The application adds references to mean-embedding vocabulary transfer and domain adaptation, while removing the Wang et al. (2019) alignment comparison. The central novelty positioning around word-level detokenization remains.

P1.justification: Section 6 is substantially rewritten from sequential input-only and input/output experiments into an explicit three-stage framework. The word/nonword discussion expands and integrates the existing prefix-control rationale, and related work gains a separate conceptual discussion. Appendices are reorganized, including moving v1 Appendix D into C.1 and its typo appendix E into D, alongside broad copyediting.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the overview and nonword-generation displays, adds a vocabulary-expansion diagram and plots for additional probing, interventions, and similarity checks, and substantially restructures Table 1. Table 5 newly displays expansion counts and token reductions. Existing prefix accuracy curves are redisplayed, while v1 Figure 6b's detailed positive-prediction panel is removed.

improvement.justification: v1 supports the FFN mechanism mainly through observational retrieval and attention patterns. v3 adds targeted-versus-random interventions affecting both reconstruction and capital recall, substantially strengthening the central mechanistic argument. Biomedical and Arabic evaluations plus measured token savings also strengthen the practical contribution. Corpus-trained refinement complicates the retained finetuning-free description, and its training budget remains ambiguous, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and methodological documentation.
